newsitem.title: USA: Black & Decker Q2 sales two pct down.
newsitem.headline: Black & Decker Q2 sales two pct down.

text.p: TOWSON, Md., July 16 - Black & Decker Corp said Wednesday its second-quarter sales dropped two percent to $1.18 billion because of the strong U.S. dollar and lower flashlight sales.

"Excluding foreign currency translation, sales were flat," said chief executive Nolan Archibald in a statement. He added SnakeLight "remained considerably lower than in the same period last year, when retailers were heavily stocking that product."
The company Wednesday reported flat second-quarter earnings of $45.5 million, or $0.47 a share, compared with $45.3 million, or $0.47 a share, the year before.
The earnings confirmed analysts' expectations. An April 18 First Call estimate of 12 brokers put Black & Decker's earnings at $0.47 a share.

With flashlight sales down for the quarter, Archibald said he expected the "difficult comparison in household products" to ease in the second half of the year. The company plans to introduce several new lighting products and the KitchenTools(TM) line of premium appliances, he added.

On the plus side, Archibald said power tools and accessories sales strengthened in the quarter, led by the company's unique DEWALT 18-volt "extreme cordless" system. He added the company's 18-volt reciprocating saw and initial shipments of a new bench and stationary tools helped sales too.

Archibald said profits in the tools and accessories sales improved "considerably" because the company's manufacturing and distribution efficiency keeps improving and its European operations benefit from restructuring.

He added sales in Black & Decker's remaining businesses were up slightly, reflecting competitive markets and weak European economies. He said profits in these businesses were generally solid, with the exception of plumbing products, which is transferring assembly operations to a lower-cost plant.

Archibald pointed out second-quarter earnings before taxes rose 13 percent to $70.1 million, from $62.1 the year before. This reflected good operating performance in most of the company's businesses and lower borrowing costs, he said.
"We are pleased with this increase, which offset our substantially higher tax rate of 35 percent, compared to 27 percent last year," he said.
